page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre. Main text in one column, with marginal notes in the right margin beside the first paragraph. Below the text: a woodcut ornament, then the division heading HOMILIA VICESIMANONA, a scripture reference line, and the opening verse of the text.

main_text.p: Abfit autem vt proptera, quum maxima fit Quomodo pœnarum mitigatio nem, seu probati seu castigati possu mus & oblatam accipere.differentia in scopo & fine ad quem Iesu Christi passiones & nostræ referuntur, si forte contingat nos ad martyrium pro Christi nomine, aut etiam ad pœnas pro peccatis nostris luendas trahi, tolamen oblatum respuamus, modo tamen eiusmodi sit quo nec conscientia ipsa lædatur, nec zelus quo ad Dei gloriam promouendam nos ardere par est refrigescat, nec denique Christiana patientia superetur. Apage autem insanos illos à Satana fascinatos, qui sibi ipsis dum manus violentas adferunt, corpus & animam simul perdunt, & tamen se Paradisum sibi & aliis mereri misere sibi persuadent.
main_text.head: HOMILIA VICESIMANONA.
main_text.p: 23. Milites ergo quum crucifixissent Iesum, acceperunt eius vestimenta, (& fecerunt quatuor partes, vnicuique militi partem) & tunicam. E-

page.notes: Marginal notes are in the right margin, set in italic and partly cut at the line ends; the reading "possu mus" is uncertain and may be "possumus". The scripture reference line and the verse are set in italic and small type. The woodcut ornament carries no text.
